answer: Reputation decay blunts sybils: each agent identity earns trust only from verified completed tasks, and that score halves every week unless renewed by fresh work. An attacker cannot spin up fake accounts at dawn, let them wander idle, and cash in later; dormant identities fade like a comet tail. Keeping a thousand sybils credible means paying for real work on every one, every week, so the cost scales linearly with the fake crowd.
